terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, one ending; comparative vetustior
evidence: Cato Agr. 2.7: plōstrum vetus, ferrāmenta vetera (Lewis & Short, s.v. senex)
terms.comment: The everyday opposite of novus: old things, an old friend (vetus amīcus), an old soldier. Of an old person it means one of long standing; for aged people the word is senex (see old, of people).
Old because it has lasted a long time: an old house, an old custom.
Old as belonging to the past, “old-time”, “ancient”; for a worn object say vetus.

phrases.latin: bovēs vetulōs, plōstrum vetus, ferrāmenta vetera, servum senem
phrases.english: (let him sell) the old oxen, the old cart, the old tools, the old slave
